Based on the provided passages, here is what each company stated regarding Medicare drug price negotiation under the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA):

**Merck (MRK)**
Merck described the IRA as making "significant changes to how drugs are covered and paid for under the Medicare program," including financial penalties for price increases exceeding inflation, a redesign of Medicare Part D, and government price-setting for Part D drugs (starting 2026) and Part B drugs (starting 2028) [2] [5]. Specifically, Merck noted that the government selected Januvia for the first year of the IRA's "Drug Price Negotiation Program," with a set price effective January 1, 2026, and selected Janumet and Janumet XR for the second year, with prices effective January 1, 2027 [4] [20]. Merck also stated that it "sued the U.S. government regarding the IRA's Program" [32]. Additionally, Merck mentioned that Lenvima was selected for price setting effective January 1, 2028, and that Keytruda is expected to be selected in 2027 for price setting effective January 1, 2029 [34] [35]. Merck also noted that government price setting may negatively impact pricing in the private market [2] [33].

**Pfizer (PFE)**
Pfizer stated that it continues to "monitor and evaluate the implementation of the IRA, including the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program (MDPNP) and its government-set Maximum Fair Price (MFP)" [30]. Pfizer noted that the MFP for Eliquis became effective on January 1, 2026, and that negotiated prices for Ibrance and Xtandi are effective in 2027 [30] [36]. Pfizer also mentioned that while Xeljanz remains a selected drug through 2028, CMS determined that bona fide marketing of a generic version still exists, so no MFP for Xeljanz will be finalized or take effect [30]. Pfizer indicated that it expects continued focus by the U.S. government on regulating drug pricing, including international reference pricing and Most-Favored-Nation (MFN) pricing [30] [36].

**Johnson & Johnson (JNJ)**
Johnson & Johnson, through its subsidiary Janssen Pharmaceuticals, Inc., stated that in July 2023, Janssen "filed litigation against the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services as well as the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services challenging the constitutionality of the IRA's Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program" [9] [13] [21]. The litigation requests a declaration that the IRA violates Janssen's rights under the First Amendment and the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution, and therefore that Janssen is not subject to the IRA's mandatory pricing scheme [9] [16] [22]. J&J noted that the impact of the IRA on its business and the broader pharmaceutical industry "remains uncertain, as litigation filed by Janssen and other pharmaceutical companies remains ongoing" [9] [16]. In April 2024, Janssen appealed the district court's denial of its summary judgment motion to the Third Circuit [9] [16], and in September 2025, a majority of the Third Circuit panel denied Janssen's appeal [22].
